property_summary: After calling transfer, the sum of token balances across all recipients should equal the amount of tokens transferred from the sender.
After calling transfer, the recipients' total received amount equals the product of the number of recipients and v (i.e., each recipient receives v tokens).
After calling transfer, the sum of all recipients' balances equals v times the number of recipients.
After transfer, the first recipient's balance increase equals v (nonzero) for the reference but 0 for the bug.

After transfer, the external call to the first recipient's address returns a boolean value that, when decoded, matches the expected success (true) for the reference but false for the bug when the recipient is an EOA and v > 0.
After calling transfer, the function returns true.
After calling transfer, the function returns the same boolean value as the original contract's return value (which is always true).
Calling transfer with valid inputs always returns true.
After calling transfer, the contract's balance remains unchanged if the call to the external address succeeds.
Calling transfer returns true when the external address is not the zero address.
All token transfers in the loop revert when the target address is not a contract.
After calling transfer, the balance of the caddress parameter should be unchanged if the token transfer reverts.
After calling transfer, the balance of the from address should not decrease by v times the number of recipients when the call is made to caddress instead of from.
The returned boolean value of transfer is always true (success), regardless of whether the internal call reverts.
The transfer function should call the caddress parameter, not the from address, so the return data from the call should be encoded with the caddress as the target.
After calling transfer, the return value of transfer is always true.
The call to transfer never reverts.
After calling transfer, the number of iterations executed equals the input _tos.length.
After transfer returns, the transaction succeeded (did not revert) only if _tos.length > 0.
After calling transfer, the value returned is always true regardless of _tos.length.
The transfer function must not revert when called with a non-empty _tos array.
The transfer function must not revert when called with valid parameters.
The transfer function must not revert when called with a non-empty _tos array.
The transfer function must not revert.
After a call to transfer on a non-empty _tos array, the return value is always true.
Every address in the _tos array receives a transferFrom call.
The number of times the return true statement is executed equals the number of elements in _tos (i.e., the loop always completes all iterations).
The function transfer executes the loop body for every element in the _tos array, i.e., it does not return early.
The return value of transfer() equals the Boolean outcome of the last call to transferFrom, or true if no call was made.
The total number of external calls made during transfer is equal to the length of the _tos array.
